header: 4Results: Transfer Gap by Rate, Method, and Target Model

images.caption:
Figure 1:Normalized context utilization of LLMLingua-2 compression by
keep-rate. English (black) declines slowly; the nine non-English
languages drop sharply betweenρ=0.75\rho=0.75andρ=0.33\rho=0.33. The
pattern replicates across both target models.

Figure 2:Mean transfer gap vs. EN atρ=0.33\rho=0.33(GPT-5.4-mini; dots =
languages). Only the learned compressor exhibits a cross-lingual gap on
GPT; budget-matched deterministic methods do not (see text for the partial
exception on Claude at this rate). This suggests the gap comes from the
compressor rather than from the task, tokenizer, or target model.

Figure 3:Transfer gap vs. EN at keep-rate 0.5 for the four learned
compressors (GPT-5.4-mini,n=300n=300). The three English-supervised
compressors show large positive gaps regardless of backbone; the
multilingually trained XProvence shows none. Kompress ZH (open marker) is
excluded from its bar: Kompress is a near no-op on Han script (achieved
rate 0.96), so its “compressed” Chinese is essentially the full context.

Figure 4:LLMLingua-2 transfer gap vs. EN atρ=0.5\rho=0.5across target
models (∗*: 95% bootstrap CI excludes 0; additional models usen=150n=150items and a reduced condition grid). The gap replicates across vendors and
model generations; Chinese is consistently hit hardest.

Figure 5:Long-context arm (150 items; target passage among 7 distractors,
question-agnostic compression). LLMLingua-2 atρ=0.33\rho=0.33keeps
English context useful but drives non-English contexts to (or below)
no-context utility for GPT; deterministic lemma+stopword compression at its
natural budget preserves 44–66% everywhere.

Figure 6:Corpus-level token premium vs. English on parallel Belebele
passages, by tokenizer. XLM-R (the compressor’s internal tokenizer) prices
the ten languages nearly equally (0.97–1.25): the compressor receives
balanced input lengths, so input length does not explain the transfer
failure. Hindi’s premium
under Qwen2.5 reaches 4.45×\times.
